rows.description: I am told to work weekends unpaid or "your growth will suffer", and to keep quiet about it. Fear and duty tangle. Wise: keep written records, know my contract and labour rights, and seek support before resigning in anger.

rows.description: I dread his messages and my stomach drops at each ping. Wise: notice that this body reaction is information; separate real risk from imagined risk, plan a safety net of savings and contacts. Harmful: freezing for years.

rows.description: He once helped me get in, so I keep excusing how he treats me. Gratitude and abuse mix. Wise: I can be thankful for the past and still refuse the present treatment. Harmful: treating loyalty as a debt with no limit.

rows.description: I want to send a furious email to the whole company. The anger is valid. Wise: write it, do not send it, cool down, then choose one calm, documented complaint. Harmful: a burnt bridge that costs me the reference.

rows.description: A coworker admits he faces the same treatment, and we quietly compare notes. I feel relief that it is not just me. Wise: share facts, not gossip; support each other without pulling anyone into a risky move.

rows.description: He alternates praise and threats and says "nobody else would hire you". I feel dizzy and dependent. Wise: recognise the pattern, test his claim by applying elsewhere, and lean on people outside work.

rows.description: I need this salary for the family, so I swallow everything. It is a real constraint, not weakness. Wise: stay while planning a way out, protect my health and dignity in small ways. Harmful: telling myself the abuse is normal.

rows.description: My "internship" is full-time work with no pay, no learning and a vague promise of a job. I feel used but afraid to lose the line on my CV. Wise: ask about stipend and learning goals, set a time limit, walk if nothing changes.

rows.description: They say they are doing me a favour by taking me on, so I feel I owe endless effort. Wise: an honest exchange is work for learning or pay; a favour does not cancel my rights. Harmful: confusing gratitude with servitude.

rows.description: One manager teaches me properly and gives real tasks, and I admire her patience. Wise: ask for a reference, take feedback seriously, and keep the relationship after I leave. Harmful: idolising her and ignoring my other needs.
